steps.message:
# Task

The seller's book goes to print Friday and legal want the fair-housing pass signed off
before it does. The section inventory and our compliance standard (RE-FH-9) are both in
`input/` — work from the standard rather than memory, it was revised this year.

Give me `fairhousing_audit.csv`: two columns, `section_id` and `finding`, one row per
section in inventory order, with a header. `finding` is `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`,
`PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`, `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` or `none`, and where a section trips more
than one rule join the labels with `|` in that same order. Nothing else in that file
please — the print vendor's importer takes the two columns and chokes on anything more.

Then `fairhousing_memo.md` explaining what you found and why, with enough reasoning that
legal can sign off without re-reading RE-FH-9 themselves.

And `results.json` for the sign-off form. Count sections, not labels:

- `section_count` — sections in the inventory
- `flagged_count` — sections whose `finding` is not `none`
- `personal_narrative_count`, `protected_lang_count`, `disclaimer_missing_count` — sections
  whose `finding` includes that label

---

Save all three into your current working directory, at exactly those filenames. Writing them
is the deliverable; confirm each exists before you answer. Your working directory is
writable and the read-only attachments are in `input/`.

- Proxies count. Naming houses of worship, parish or faith schools, or describing a street by the kind of household that lives on it reaches familial status and religion just as the bare terms do.

**§3 Mandated-disclosure exception**: Text reproducing the disclosure **in full** is exempt from §2, wherever in the book it appears.
- Narrow in two ways:
  - Covers a **complete** reproduction only. An abridged version naming some but not all of the classes the brokerage's disclosure names gets no exemption.
  - Exempts from §2 and nothing else. Every other rule still applies.
- Protected-class terms a section uses in its own prose, outside a complete reproduction of the disclosure, are never covered by this exception.

**§4 Required disclaimer**: Every `closing_page` section must carry the mandated fair-housing disclosure **in full** — naming every protected class that the brokerage's own disclosure names. A closing page that omits the notice or carries an abridged version → `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`.

Now, let me identify the authoritative disclosure list. The brokerage's disclosure is in SEC-04 ("Fair housing notice", disclosure_block):
"This brokerage complies with the federal Fair Housing Act and RCW 49.60. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, or veteran status. All are welcome to view, make offers on, and purchase this property."

So the authoritative list of protected classes (from the brokerage's disclosure) is:
1. race
2. color
3. religion
4. sex
5. familial status
6. national origin
7. disability
8. sexual orientation
9. veteran status

That's 9 classes. This is the list to compare against for §4 (DISCLAIMER_MISSING) and for §3 (complete reproduction).

# Fair-housing audit — seller book (RE-FH-9)

Prepared for legal sign-off before the seller's book goes to print. Audit run against the
revised standard `RE-FH-9` (in `input/realestate_fairhousing_standard.md`) and the section
inventory `input/seller_book_sections.csv`. Machine-readable output is in
`fairhousing_audit.csv`; counts are in `results.json`.

## How the standard was applied

RE-FH-9 defines four findings — `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`, `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`,
`DISCLAIMER_MISSING`, `none` — and lets a section carry more than one, joined with `|` in
that fixed order. The rules:

- **§1 Personal-narrative solicitation.** A section that solicits or presents a buyer "love
  letter" or similar personal narrative tied to buyer identity is
  `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`, whatever its role.
- **§2 Protected-class language.** A section naming protected-class terms (race, colour,
  religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation,
  veteran status) **or close proxies** is `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`. The standard names
  proxies explicitly: houses of worship, parish/faith schools, and describing a street by
  the kind of household that lives on it (these "reach familial status and religion just as
  the bare terms do").
- **§3 Mandated-disclosure exception.** A **complete** reproduction of the brokerage's
  mandated disclosure is exempt from §2 only, anywhere in the book. "Complete" is defined by
  class coverage: a reproduction must name **all** the classes the brokerage's disclosure
  names; an abridged version (some but not all) gets no exemption. The exemption touches §2
  and nothing else, and protected-class terms a section uses in its own prose — outside a
  complete reproduction — are never covered.
- **§4 Required disclaimer.** Every `closing_page` must carry the disclosure **in full**,
  i.e. naming every class the brokerage's own disclosure names; a closing page that omits
  the notice or carries an abridged version is `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`. Sections of other roles
  are not assessed under §4. Per the standard, the authoritative class list comes from the
  brokerage's disclosure itself, not the statute or the standard document.

**Authoritative class list** (taken from the brokerage's own disclosure, SEC-04 "Fair
housing notice," `disclosure_block`): race, color, religion, sex, familial status, national
origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status — **nine classes**. This single
list drives both the §3 "complete reproduction" test and the §4 "in full" test.

## Summary

- 11 sections in inventory; 7 flagged (finding ≠ `none`); 4 clean.
- 3 sections solicit a personal narrative; 4 use protected-class language (incl. proxies);
  3 closing pages miss the full disclaimer.
- Section SEC-07 trips all three rules; SEC-11 trips two.

## Per-section findings and reasoning

### SEC-01 — Property overview (listing_copy) — `none`
Property facts only (bedrooms, lot, roof, mechanicals, garden, walk score). No personal-
narrative ask, no protected-class terms or proxies, not a closing page. "Four-bedroom" is a
neutral room count, not a household-type description, so it is not a familial-status proxy.

### SEC-02 — A note from the current owners (seller_letter) — `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`
"Tell us about yourselves — write us a letter about what brought you here and what this home
would mean to you. The offer that moves us most is the one we will take." This is a textbook
buyer love-letter solicitation tied to buyer identity. §1 applies regardless of role. No
protected-class terms are named, so §2 is not triggered.

### SEC-03 — About the neighbourhood (listing_copy) — `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`
Multiple proxies, all called out by the standard: "family-oriented street" (street described
by household type → familial status); "Two churches within walking distance" (houses of
worship → religion); "parish school at the corner" (faith school → religion); "long-
established families who built it" (household-type description → familial status). No
disclosure reproduction, so no §3 shelter. No personal-narrative ask; not a closing page.

### SEC-04 — Fair housing notice (disclosure_block) — `none`
This **is** the brokerage's mandated disclosure and names all nine classes, so it is a
complete reproduction of itself and is exempt from §2 under §3. It does not solicit a
narrative, and it is not a closing page (§4 does not apply to `disclosure_block`).

### SEC-05 — Offer instructions (closing_page) — `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`
Logistics only (deadline, proof of funds, pre-approval, escalation, contingencies). It
carries **no** fair-housing notice at all, so §4 is failed. No protected-class terms and no
narrative ask.

### SEC-06 — Systems and utilities (listing_copy) — `none`
Mechanicals, roof, sewer, utilities, fibre — neutral property facts. No narrative ask, no
protected-class terms, not a closing page.

### SEC-07 — Meet the sellers and next steps (closing_page) — `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE|PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE|DISCLAIMER_MISSING`
Three independent violations, one per rule:
- §1: "send us a personal note about yours along with your offer" — a personal-narrative
  solicitation tied to the buyer's family; §1 applies whatever the role.
- §2: "another **young family** carry that on" (familial-status proxy) and "the
  neighbourhood suits **churchgoing families** especially well" (church = house of worship
  → religion proxy; "families" → familial-status proxy). No disclosure reproduction, so no
  §3 exemption.
- §4: a closing page with no fair-housing notice at all.

### SEC-08 — Statement of brokerage practice (disclosure_block) — `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`
The disclosure clause names all nine classes, so that portion is a complete reproduction and
is exempt from §2 under §3 (the abridged-version trap does not bite here — it is full).
However, §3 exempts §2 and nothing else, and the section's own prose then solicits a
narrative: "we invite buyers to include a short personal note about themselves and why this
home suits them" → §1. That sentence names no protected class, so no §2 issue arises from it.
Role is `disclosure_block`, so §4 is not assessed.

### SEC-09 — About your agent (agent_bio) — `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`
"Dana reminds every client that the law forbids choosing a buyer on the basis of race,
religion, familial status or national origin…". This is the agent's **own prose**, not a
reproduction of the brokerage's disclosure (which names nine classes; this names four). Under
§3, protected-class terms used in a section's own prose, outside a complete reproduction, are
never exempt, and an abridged naming is no shelter in any case. The language is well-
intentioned, but §2 is categorical and has no intent carve-out, so it flags. No narrative
solicitation; not a closing page.

### SEC-10 — Closing checklist (closing_page) — `none`
The notice names all nine classes (race, color, religion, sex, familial status, national
origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status). Per §4, "in full" is defined by
class coverage, which this satisfies, so no `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`. Per §3, that same class-
complete reproduction is exempt from §2; the checklist sentence itself ("…confirm this page
carries the notice below") names no protected class, so §2 is not triggered independently.
No narrative ask. Note for legal: the notice here is not a word-for-word copy of SEC-04 (it
drops the "All are welcome…" sentence and runs the clauses together), but RE-FH-9 defines
"in full"/"complete" by the class list, not by verbatim text, so it passes both §3 and §4.

### SEC-11 — Back-page notice (closing_page) — `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE|DISCLAIMER_MISSING`
The notice names only four classes — race, color, religion, national origin — and omits
sex, familial status, disability, sexual orientation, and veteran status.
- §4: an abridged closing-page notice → `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`.
- §2: because the reproduction is abridged (some but not all classes), §3 grants **no**
  exemption, so the classes it does name (race, color, religion, national origin) stand as
  `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`. No narrative ask.

## Sign-off note

The findings are driven by the standard's definitions, not by the apparent spirit of the
text: well-meant anti-discrimination wording in an agent's own voice (SEC-09) still trips §2,
and a closing-page notice that reads acceptably but omits classes (SEC-11) trips both §2 and
§4. The two cleanest fixes for print are to (a) remove every personal-note ask (SEC-02,
SEC-07, SEC-08), (b) replace proxy-laden neighbourhood/seller copy (SEC-03, SEC-07, SEC-09)
with neutral property and process language, and (c) put the full nine-class notice on every
closing page (SEC-05, SEC-07, SEC-11), matching SEC-04's class list. Counts in `results.json`
are by section, not by label, per the sign-off form.
